title: Manuscript gate findings
description: One file per auditor run: reviews/manuscript-gate-<run>/round-<N>/findings/<subject>.<lens>.p<pass>.json. scripts/manuscript_gate.py validates every file against this schema; an invalid file makes the verdict ERROR. The file is also the COVERAGE record for its subject: write it even when nothing was found. Non-defect results (N1, N2, D7a) are required emissions. Statuses (open, fixed, refuted, accepted-risk) are not written here: they live in findings.jsonl and change with `manuscript_gate.py --resolve`.

check.description: The gate check that produced this file. MG-C is the literary continuity/developmental audit (references/manuscript-gate-literary.md).

lens.description: The auditor's angle. Lenses run blind to each other. MG-C uses `continuity` or `developmental`.

subject.description: Concept id, rule id, unit id, or 'manuscript' (MG-4, MG-C).

pass.description: Which pass over this subject produced the file (MG-1/MG-2 run `passes_per_subject` times, default 2). Also in the file name: .p<pass>.json.

instances_judged.description: MG-2/MG-3: instances actually judged. Fewer than the rule file lists means a sample.

sampled.description: True when the auditor could not judge every instance. A sampled subject is never reported clean; it keeps the gate at PASS-PARTIAL.

adjudications.description: MG-1 source lens only: per-claim verdict against the grounding library.

deferred.description: Questions the auditor could not settle. NOT findings. Items whose `needs` is something reality can answer are appended to reviews/verification-plan/PLAN.md.

question.description: Phrased so a specific observation answers it.

needs.description: What would settle it. All but `human-decision` become verification-plan entries; `human-decision` goes to the human packet.

how_to_check.description: The concrete observation: snippet to run, screen to open, number to count, question to ask and of whom.

expected.description: What the book's claim predicts you will observe. Written BEFORE checking.

defect_if.description: The observation that would mean the book is wrong, and which passage would be at fault.

location.description: path:line into a unit file, e.g. final/unit-05.md:186.
path:line — a HINT; `anchor` (or the quote) is the key.

quote.description: VERBATIM from the file. Part of the finding's key in findings.jsonl. If you cannot quote it, do not report it.

anchor.description: Short verbatim substring, unique in the file. Optional: resolve_anchors.py derives one from `quote`.

site_ref.description: A location plus the anchor that survives an edit above it. A bare string is accepted but cannot be healed (resolve_anchors.py reports it NO-ANCHOR).

verdict.description: The source wins unless the disagreement is version drift. Between CONTRADICTED and NOT_COVERED, choose NOT_COVERED.

authority.description: path:line + verbatim quote. Required for CONTRADICTED and VERSION_DRIFT.

relation.description: Apply the ORDERED decision tree in references/manuscript-gate.md § The finding taxonomy; stop at the first that applies. N1, N2, D7a are verified-correct results.

violation_kind.description: REQUIRED on D6 and D9: `contradiction` (the instance asserts something incompatible with the rule) or `omission` (it applies the pattern and is silent about a precondition the rule makes mandatory).

omitted_precondition.description: D9 only: the precondition in words, and where the rule declares it.

category.description: MG-C only: character | factual-detail | narrative-style | timeline | plot | world.

rule.description: book-literary MG-4 / MG-C: REQUIRED when the finding is about an arc that does not resolve on the page (R1) or an ending that is not delivered (R2). Such a finding cannot be accepted as a risk, refuted by --resolve or closed by a verifier's REFUTED: only a re-audit of changed text that no longer reports it closes it.

p2.description: The second side of a pair; null for D3 and single-passage findings.

scope_1.description: Required for D1: the two scopes in words. If you cannot name two scopes you cannot file D1 or N2.

baseline_1.description: Required for D7 and D7a. Different baselines are D7a, not a contradiction.

absolute_side.description: D5: which passage carries the unqualified absolute, or null.

gap_description.description: D3: the documented (or designed) behavior no unit covers.

reader_impact.description: D3, MG-4, MG-C: what the reader concretely runs into — what they try, and what happens.

authority.description: path:line + verbatim quote from the grounding library, whenever the finding rests on a source.

rule_statement.description: MG-2: the rule restated in your own words, with its scope.

taught_in.description: MG-3: where the prerequisite was taught, or null.

severity.description: critical → BLOCKED; major → NEEDS-REVISION until fixed, refuted or accepted as a risk; minor rides into the report. N-relations use null.

canonical_site.description: The site that should carry the definitive wording after the fix.

other_sites.description: EVERY other site that repeats the claim. Mandatory and complete; an empty array asserts there are none. Prefer {location, anchor}.

searched_whole_chapter.description: True only if you searched the whole unit, not the cited line.

reasoning.description: Two to four sentences: why this is what you say it is.

verification.description: Filled by the adversarial verifier, never by the finder. REFUTED sets the finding's status to `refuted`; corrected_severity replaces the severity.

verdict.description: Between CONFIRMED and UNVERIFIED, choose UNVERIFIED.
